definition: to examine something in detail in order to understand it
example: It is important to analyse the causes of climate change before proposing solutions.

definition: a way of dealing with or thinking about something
example: Schools should adopt a more practical approach to teaching science.

definition: a particular part of a subject, activity, or place
example: Renewable energy is an area where significant investment is needed.

definition: to evaluate or estimate the value, quality, or extent of something
example: Teachers should assess students based on a range of skills, not just exam results.

definition: to accept something as true without proof
example: Many people assume that technology always makes life easier.

definition: the power or right to give orders and make decisions, or an official organization
example: Local authorities are responsible for maintaining public parks.

definition: able to be used or obtained
example: Free healthcare should be available to everyone, regardless of income.

definition: an advantage or profit gained from something
example: One major benefit of remote work is a better work-life balance.

definition: an abstract idea or general notion
example: The concept of sustainable development has become central to modern policy-making.

definition: to be composed or made up of something
example: A balanced diet should consist of fruits, vegetables, and whole grains.

definition: to form or make up a whole
example: Young people constitute a large proportion of social media users.

definition: the circumstances that form the setting for an event or idea
example: It's important to consider historical context when studying a country's laws.

definition: a written or spoken agreement, especially one intended to be enforceable by law
example: Employees should read their contract carefully before signing.

definition: to bring something into existence
example: Automation has created new job opportunities in some industries while eliminating others.

definition: facts and statistics collected for reference or analysis
example: The report is based on data collected from over 1,000 households.

definition: to state the exact meaning or nature of something
example: It can be difficult to define success in purely financial terms.

definition: to obtain or trace something from a particular source
example: Many English words derive from Latin and Greek.

definition: to give something out to a number of people
example: The charity distributes food to families in need every week.

definition: the system of trade, industry, and money in a country
example: A strong economy depends on both consumer spending and government investment.

definition: the natural world, or the surrounding conditions in which someone lives or works
example: Businesses are under growing pressure to protect the environment.

definition: to set up or create something on a firm basis
example: The company was established over fifty years ago.

definition: to roughly calculate a value, number, or extent
example: Experts estimate that global temperatures will rise by two degrees by 2050.

definition: clearly seen or understood; obvious
example: It is evident that public transport reduces traffic congestion.

definition: to send goods to another country for sale
example: The country exports most of its agricultural products to Europe.

definition: a circumstance or fact that contributes to a result
example: Diet is just one factor that affects a person's overall health.

definition: the management of money, especially by governments or organizations
example: Poor financial planning can lead to serious problems later in life.

definition: a fixed method or set of principles for doing something
example: There is no single formula for a happy and successful life.

definition: the purpose or role of something
example: The main function of a school is to prepare students for adult life.

definition: to recognize or establish who or what something is
example: The first step in solving a problem is to identify its cause.

definition: money received, especially from work or investment
example: Higher education is often linked to higher income later in life.

definition: to point out or show something
example: Recent studies indicate that remote work can increase productivity.

definition: a single person, as distinct from a group
example: The policy should take into account the needs of each individual.

definition: to explain or understand the meaning of something
example: Different cultures may interpret the same behavior in very different ways.

definition: to include something as a necessary part
example: Raising a child involves far more than simply providing food and shelter.

definition: an important topic for debate, or a problem
example: Climate change is one of the most pressing issues of our time.

definition: work, especially physical or manual work
example: Many factories rely on cheap labour to keep production costs low.

definition: relating to the law
example: There should be legal consequences for companies that pollute rivers.

definition: to make laws
example: Governments must legislate to reduce carbon emissions.

definition: important, significant, or serious
example: Pollution is a major cause of respiratory illness in cities.

definition: a particular way of doing something
example: Online learning is becoming a popular method of education.

definition: to happen or take place
example: Most traffic accidents occur due to driver distraction.

definition: one part in every hundred
example: Over sixty percent of the population now lives in urban areas.

definition: a length or portion of time
example: The economy grew steadily over a five-year period.

definition: a course of action adopted by a government, business, or organization
example: The government introduced a new policy to reduce plastic waste.

definition: a fundamental rule, truth, or belief
example: Fairness is one of the key principles of a good education system.

definition: to continue with a course of action
example: The construction project will proceed despite public objections.

definition: a series of actions taken to achieve a particular result
example: Recycling reduces waste through an efficient process of reusing materials.

definition: to need something for a particular purpose
example: Most professional jobs now require a university degree.

definition: the systematic study of a subject to discover facts or reach conclusions
example: Further research is needed to fully understand the effects of social media on teenagers.

definition: to reply or react to something
example: Governments must respond quickly to natural disasters.

definition: the function or position someone or something has
example: Parents play a crucial role in a child's early education.

definition: a distinct part of something larger
example: This section of the report focuses on renewable energy.

definition: a distinct part of the economy, society, or an activity
example: The tourism sector was severely affected by the pandemic.

definition: important or notable enough to have an effect
example: There has been a significant improvement in air quality since the new regulations.

definition: resembling something else without being identical
example: Many developed countries face similar challenges with an aging population.

definition: a place, person, or thing from which something originates
example: Solar power is a clean source of energy.

definition: clearly defined or particular, as distinct from general
example: The training program targets specific skills needed in the job market.

definition: the way in which parts of something are organized or arranged
example: The company changed its management structure to improve efficiency.

definition: a system of ideas intended to explain something
example: There are several theories about why some students perform better than others.

definition: to differ or change from one instance to another
example: Working hours vary greatly between different countries and industries.
